detailedExplanation: This topic is verified against The Tiffin Girls’ School Year 9 Biology Curriculum Outline 2026–27 and the corresponding AQA GCSE Biology 8461 content.

Metabolism includes respiration and also reactions that build or break down molecules. Examples include converting glucose to storage molecules, forming lipids from glycerol and fatty acids, using glucose and nitrate ions to make amino acids in plants, and breaking down excess amino acids to form urea in the liver.
A key idea is that respiration transfers energy that can be used to drive many other metabolic reactions.
